key_insight: VesNet replaces the most expensive near-field vesicle interaction calculations with a neural approximation, while keeping the rest of the Stokes-flow solver physics-based.
engineering_relevance: This hybrid approach makes large-scale vesicle suspension simulation much faster, enabling practical studies of deformable particle flows on modest hardware.
method: Neural network predicts vesicle self-interactions, including background-flow coupling and short-range lubrication forces.
Conventional modules still handle boundary reparameterization and far-field hydrodynamics.
GPU implementation accelerates the solver for 2D Stokesian vesicle suspensions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports over 100x speedup versus a multithreaded MATLAB CPU boundary-integral solver and about 5x versus its GPU counterpart, while matching key dynamics in single-vesicle, pair, and many-vesicle tests.
watch_item: The method is presented for two-dimensional vesicle suspensions, so extending accuracy and robustness to fully three-dimensional, more complex geometries may require additional validation.
paper_title: VesNet: Neural network accelerated solver for simulating Stokesian vesicle suspensions
